paper_summary: Al99.5 matrix syntactic foams filled with 64 vol% Al2O3 ceramic hollow spheres (2.24+/-0.13 mm diameter) were produced by liquid-state low-pressure vacuum infiltration, with the aluminium matrix itself reinforced by 0.6 mm nominal size SiC particles at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 vol% relative to the matrix volume (0-8.76 vol% of the total volume). Microscopy and EDS showed uniform infiltration with no reaction products, and standardized ISO 13314 compression tests showed that specific compressive strength and specific structural stiffness rose in every reinforced case (up to 49.3 MPa*cm3/g, a 63.2+/-8.1% gain over the unreinforced foam, and +34.5% stiffness at 30 vol% SiC). Specific plateau strength and specific energy absorption only improved at 15 vol% SiC and above, because at 5-10 vol% the SiC particles acted as stress concentrators during plastic collapse; failure was by plastic collapse followed by cleavage-band formation and widening.

structure.microstructure_notes: Relative density (sample density / matrix density) = 0.622 +/- (see Table 1); measured density computed as rho_rel x 2.7 g/cm3. Optical/SEM/EDS showed uniform matrix infiltration with no agglomeration, no matrix penetration into the CHSs and no reaction products at the CHS/matrix or SiC/matrix interfaces. CHS bulk density reported as 0.87 +/- 0.08 g/cm3.

extraction_notes: All seven compositions are fully tabulated in Appendix C (absolute properties) and Appendix D (specific properties), so every record carries measured values. Field mapping: strength_mpa = compressive strength sigma_C (stress at the first peak after the elastic region); plateau_stress_mpa = sigma_PLT (mean stress between 20% and 40% strain); energy_absorption_mj_m3 = W50, the area under the engineering stress-strain curve to 50% strain, reported in J/cm3, which equals MJ/m3 exactly (no numerical conversion needed); modulus_mpa = the ISO 13314 structural stiffness S, i.e. the slope of the initial linear part of the engineering stress-strain curve, which is a structural stiffness rather than a true Young's modulus; specific_strength_mpa_per_g_cc = sigma_C/rho and specific_modulus_mpa_per_g_cc = S/rho from Table D1. measured_density_g_cc was computed as the stated relative density (Table 1) multiplied by the stated Al99.5 matrix density of 2.7 g/cm3; this is consistent to within 0.01 g/cm3 with sigma_C divided by sigma_C/rho for every sample. particle_volume_fraction = 0.64 is the CHS filler content, constant for all samples; the varying SiC content is a matrix reinforcement (a solid, not hollow, particle) and is therefore recorded in additional_fillers, giving both the vol% relative to the matrix and the vol% of the total volume as stated on p. 379. strain_rate_per_s = 0.002 was converted from the stated 3 mm/min crosshead speed on a 25 mm cube (3/60/25 s^-1). Test temperature was not stated and is assumed to be room temperature (25 C). The CHS 'bulk density' of 0.87+/-0.08 g/cm3 is ambiguous (it does not reconcile with the measured foam densities under a simple rule of mixtures, suggesting it is a packed/tap density rather than a single-sphere true density), so particle_true_density_g_cc was left null and the value is recorded in microstructure_notes instead. Standard deviations are given in the paper but the schema has no field for them, so only mean values are stored; the evidence quotes are condensed table rows because the source tables were flattened to one cell per line during PDF text extraction. Process route is recorded as pressure_infiltration: molten metal was driven in by 500 kPa argon after a 10^-4 Pa vacuum was established, i.e. vacuum-assisted pressure infiltration. cure_or_process_temperature_c = 750 C is the infiltration hold temperature (after 1.5 h at 600 C). Stress-drop magnitudes after the first peak (6.3+/-1.3 MPa unreinforced, 22.8+/-5.6 MPa reinforced average) and the fitted linear property-vs-vol% equations have no schema field and were not recorded.
